findings.label: auditor-setup-contradiction
findings.summary: The auditor launch is contradicted by the stated setup guards.
findings.detail: auditor-setting requires launch_auditor/4 to set KOGEN_ROLE=auditor, but the same contract says both setup guards refuse KOGEN_ROLE=auditor. If launch uses either adapter's setup path, every auditor launch fails and the paid auditor observations are impossible. Define guards that reject auditor only for non-auditor entrypoints, or add a dedicated auditor setup path accepted by launch_auditor/4, and prove the complete launch.

findings.label: write-policy-contradiction
findings.summary: The auditor materialization ownership policy permits and rejects the same writes.
findings.detail: risks.yaml says the materialization's permitted mutation is 'Only inside .git/' and rejects changes elsewhere, while blind-auditor-layer says every write, including inside .git/, rejects the session. This leaves the Developer with no exact write policy and can make a correct implementation fail or permit writes unexpectedly. Change the ownership rule to permit no writes anywhere and retain the full .git manifest check, then make the tests and prompt use that single rule.

findings.label: live-target-contract-incomplete
findings.summary: The two paid targets omit required fixture authentication and preflight contracts.
findings.detail: live-shaping-quality names the codex route and a fast auditor profile but does not specify the fixture's Shaper profile, login/setup mechanism, or preflight commands. live-shape-to-build likewise names only the default route and fast auditor profile, with no exact login or preflight contract. A target can therefore run with the wrong route/auth or skip required preflights while still satisfying the stated observation. Add exact fixture route, every profile, login/setup, preflights, per-case/module budget, and receipt assertions showing the claimed observation.

findings.label: root-idle-proof-blind
findings.summary: The proofs do not observe the central root-idle and front-loaded-question requirements.
findings.detail: Offline checks mostly assert prompt substrings and launch arguments; the live integrity description checks recorded picker questions and auditor roots, but not root tool calls, helper-start ordering, or elapsed time to the first question. A plausible controller that researches/probes in the root, delays its first question, or never launches the required helpers can pass the proofs while violating the contract. Instrument the harness/evaluation transcript to assert helper launches precede root work, the first eligible question is prompt-front-loaded, and post-window questions are absent.
